headline: USAR REBOUNDS 11% FROM EARNINGS ROUT — MP MATERIALS +4%, JEFFERIES HOLDS $21 BUY ON SERRA VERDE THESIS
snippet: USA Rare Earth (Nasdaq: USAR) surged 11% on November 11 to approximately $8.82, fully reversing its Monday post-earnings collapse, as Jefferies reiterated its Buy rating and $21 target — calling Serra Verde reaching 4,000 tonnes per year by Q2 2027 the key litmus test for the thesis. MP Materials (NYSE: MP) climbed 4% to $38 as Freedom Broker initiated coverage with a Buy rating, while United States Antimony edged higher in sympathy; the broad sector rebound confirms Monday's selloff was fear-driven rather than a re-rating of the underlying rare earth supply-chain narrative.

headline: AWALÉ DRILLS 10.6 G/T GOLD OVER 57M IN CÔTE D'IVOIRE — CHARGER 1 AND 2 MERGE INTO ONE CONTINUOUS SYSTEM
snippet: Awalé Resources (TSX-V: ARIC) reported that holes confirming 10.6 g/t gold over 57 metres from 150 metres below surface and 210 metres along strike from discovery holes have demonstrated that the previously separate Charger 1 and Charger 2 zones have merged into one continuous mineralized system at its Odienné project in Côte d'Ivoire. The geological significance is substantial: a system already hosting exceptional grades across a 1,542 km² land package is now proven to be spatially continuous, increasing the probability that a large-scale gold deposit exists and potentially simplifying the future resource estimation process.

headline: THACKER PASS COSTS JUMP 31% TO $3.83B — LITHIUM AMERICAS SHARES CRATER 8% ON LABOUR AND LOGISTICS CREEP
snippet: Lithium Americas (TSX: LAC) disclosed that Phase 1 capital costs for its Thacker Pass project in Nevada have risen approximately 31% to $3.83 billion, driven by higher labour, construction and logistics expenses beyond the $80-120 million tariff-driven revision disclosed earlier in 2026 — sending shares down nearly 8% in Toronto trading. The revision raises new questions about project economics at a time when lithium carbonate prices remain below the levels assumed in the company's original feasibility study, and extends a pattern of cost escalation that began when Phase 1 capex was increased from $2.27 billion to $2.93 billion in 2025.

headline: INDIA BANS LITHIUM BATTERY BLACK MASS EXPORTS — SOVEREIGN RESOURCE MOVE LOCKS IN 4 CRITICAL MINERALS
snippet: India banned on November 11 the export of lithium-ion battery black mass — the recycled material derived from end-of-life batteries containing lithium, cobalt, nickel and manganese — a policy mirroring China's approach to critical mineral resource nationalism and aimed at keeping strategic battery feedstocks within India's domestic supply chain. The ban adds pressure to European and North American battery recyclers who relied on Indian-origin feedstocks, and signals that the race to secure battery material supply chains is intensifying among major battery manufacturing regions beyond China.

headline: GREAT BOULDER HITS 39.9 G/T OVER 8M AT GOLDEN TREASURE — BEST-EVER RESULT AHEAD OF RESOURCE UPDATE, PEAK HILL WA
snippet: Great Boulder Resources (ASX: GBR) reported its best-ever intersection at Golden Treasure within its Peak Hill gold project in Western Australia — 8 metres at 39.9 g/t gold — ahead of a planned maiden resource estimate. The high-grade hit confirms the discovery area can support an underground mining scenario, with the exceptional grade placing Golden Treasure among the highest-grade undeveloped gold targets in the state's historically productive Murchison goldfield.

headline: ROX RESOURCES DRILLS 15.13 G/T OVER 4.87M AT YOUANMI — 25M BELOW KNOWN RESOURCE, GRADE ZONE OPEN AT DEPTH
snippet: Rox Resources (ASX: RXL) reported a 4.87-metre intersection grading 15.13 g/t gold at Youanmi, located approximately 25 metres below the base of the current mineral resource, extending a high-grade gold system in Western Australia's Murchison region that hosts one of the state's most prospective undeveloped high-grade development targets. The result confirms the deposit remains open at depth and that high-grade mineralization continues below the current resource footprint, supporting the case for a resource upgrade.

headline: GBM RESOURCES DRILLS 50M AT 2.01 G/T AT LONE SISTER — WIDE OPEN-PITTABLE INTERCEPT BUILDS RESOURCE CASE, QLD
snippet: GBM Resources (ASX: GBM) reported 50 metres grading 2.01 g/t gold at its Lone Sister prospect within the Mt Coolon Gold Project in central Queensland, a wide intercept consistent with open-pit scale bulk-tonnage mineralization rather than narrow high-grade veins. The result adds to a growing body of step-out holes confirming the breadth of the mineralized system, with the company testing multiple targets within a consolidated central Queensland land package that could support a larger resource than currently defined.

headline: CAMECO FALLS 10% ON Q3 MISS AS URANIUM EQUITIES COOL — 19-YEAR PRICE HIGH CANNOT LIFT BEATEN-DOWN STOCKS
snippet: An Admiral Markets analysis of uranium stocks in November 2026 examines why equities including Cameco (NYSE: CCJ) and Denison Mines have significantly underperformed spot uranium prices this year, even as the commodity recently touched a 19-year high near $91/lb. Cameco fell approximately 10% following its Q3 2026 earnings report as the company narrowed its full-year production and sales outlook with lower nine-month profit, and the broader uranium complex has pulled back 30-50% from 2026 peaks — a gap that analysts attribute to investor rotation, profit-taking after a multi-year run, and AI data-centre sentiment concerns rather than any change in the long-run nuclear supply-demand balance.

headline: NORTHERN MINER: 4 US JUNIORS DRILL FOR SCALE IN WYOMING, NEVADA — RIDGELINE SELLS 4 PROPERTIES TO BARRICK-NEWMONT JV FOR $23.2M
snippet: The Northern Miner profiles four US-focused junior exploration companies drilling for discovery-scale targets in November 2026, highlighting Relevant Gold's high-grade drill program at Bradley Peak and Lewiston in central Wyoming as a jurisdiction investors are increasingly looking at amid elevated permitting timelines in Canada. The piece also notes the M&A validation angle: Ridgeline Minerals sold four Nevada gold exploration properties to Nevada Gold Mines, the Barrick-Newmont joint venture, for $23.2 million in August 2026 — a concrete data point that junior exploration success in Nevada now has a clear institutional exit pathway as the majors accelerate their reserve replacement.

headline: DALAROO METALS DRILLS 2.67 G/T OVER 13M AT WILFRED — GOLD HIT 1.25KM FROM DISCOVERY CONFIRMS SYSTEM SCALE
snippet: Dalaroo Metals (ASX: DAL) reported 13 metres averaging 2.67 g/t gold at its Wilfred gold project, struck approximately 1.25 kilometres from the original discovery section — a step-out distance that confirms the mineralized system is significantly larger than the initial footprint suggested. The company is now testing the full strike extent across a district-scale land package in a geological setting consistent with large-scale gold endowment, and the successful distal hole changes the exploration model from a focused target to a potentially camp-scale system.
